selected.rationale: A loss on the basket checkout integration event can silently prevent downstream order creation, exposing missing publisher confirmation or outbox-based retry defenses.
Dropping order-submission requests causes checkout failure or duplicate orders if clients retry, revealing a lack of idempotency or retry on the critical ordering API edge.
Latency into Basket.API on the user's cart/checkout path may propagate unbounded delay to the WebApp, exposing missing timeouts or fail-fast behavior.
Losing connectivity to the Redis basket store makes the customer's basket unavailable and can abort checkout, exposing a direct availability and recovery weakness.
Delay on the mobile order placement path affects the mobile checkout experience and can expose missing timeout/retry protection in the BFF-to-ordering edge.
Slow identity API responses can stall authentication/authorization across the web app, revealing missing timeout and circuit-breaking defenses on the identity dependency.
Loss of Basket.API requests prevents users from loading or updating their cart, exposing missing retry/fallback behavior in a synchronous user-facing dependency.
Loss of catalog responses breaks product browsing and checkout item rendering, exposing the absence of fallback or retry for the catalog API.
